query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Substitution of 10% of the ferromagnetic elements in magnetic high-entropy alloys with dysprosium will increase the coercive field by 30% relative to the baseline as-cast alloy at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure, due to the increased magnetic anisotropy and modified exchange interactions.
generation.intervention: substitution of 10% of the ferromagnetic elements with dysprosium
generation.mechanism: increased magnetic anisotropy and modified exchange interactions due to dysprosium substitution
generation.boundary: room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure
generation.uncertainty: the actual increase in coercive field may vary depending on the specific composition of the alloy and the processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: prepare a series of magnetic high-entropy alloys with varying amounts of dysprosium substitution, measure the coercive field at room temperature and standard atmospheric pressure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the coercive field does not increase by at least 20% for the alloy with 10% dysprosium substitution, the hypothesis is falsified
